3code - RAM usage analysis

October 30, 2026. Measurements from the ram worktree at 54cddeda (release config, -d:release --opt:size, ORC, Nim 2.4.0), Linux 6.x, glibc. Reproducible with tests/tty/probe_ram.nim (new) and tests/api/test_memory_leak.nim (extended to print its numbers).

The short version

A 3code session costs about 10 MB resident at boot and grows with the history it keeps in memory, roughly 160 kB per turn before compaction. Auto-summarization bounds the history, and measured RSS slope after warmup is 16 kB over 90 turns in the 120-turn threaded-transport regression (test_memory_leak, issue #35), i.e. flat. Real working sessions on this box sit between 20 MB and 205 MB depending on how much conversation and tool output they carry.

The big VSZ numbers in top (300-500 MB) are not memory usage: two glibc thread arenas each reserve 64 MB of address space (PROT_NONE, zero pages touched), plus an 8 MB thread stack reservation, plus the usual library mappings. RSS is the number that costs anything.

Live sessions (the "why is 3code using X" table)

Sampled from /proc/<pid>/status of real sessions on this machine, real providers, October 30 around 12:52:

PIDUptimeThreadsVSZRSS
892149~1.4 h3303 MB20 MB
860922~2 h4355 MB62 MB
961863~1.3 h6346 MB63 MB
1071766~1.2 h4520 MB156 MB
885992~1.5 h4515 MB205 MB

All five were flat over a 2-minute re-sample: the big ones had grown during active turns (long conversations, tool output, streaming buffers) and were steady once idle. Idle drift over 75 s in the controlled probe below was exactly zero kB.

A debugger note for anyone reproducing this: gdb -p on a foreign 3code fails under ptrace_scope=1 (siblings cannot trace siblings), and distro glibc strips malloc_stats/malloc_info from the exported symbol table, so they are not debugger-callable either. The census below comes from /proc/<pid>/smaps of a self-spawned child, which an ancestor may read.

Controlled probe: boot, idle, turns, paste, resume

tests/tty/probe_ram.nim drives the real binary (built with -d:providerStub, so the model is canned but the full UI, editor, render, thread, and session machinery is live) through a PTY and samples /proc/<pid> at each stage. 119x40 terminal, 40 turns, one 8 kB paste, then exit and -r resume of the same session:

StageRSSVSZThreads
boot, prompt ready9.7 MB21.8 MB2
after 75 s idle9.7 MB21.8 MB2
turn 514.1 MB164.2 MB3
turn 4016.0 MB165.7 MB3
8 kB paste in editor18.6 MB168.3 MB3
paste submitted18.7 MB168.3 MB3
resume, 14 kB .3log10.0 MB22.3 MB2

Reading the table:

  • The first five turns retain ~4.4 MB (message history, rendered rows, receipts) and add one thread (the network worker); VSZ jumps ~142 MB at that point because glibc sizes the worker's arena reservation then, not at boot. RSS barely moves.
  • Turns retain history: about 160 kB/turn with the stub's ~3.7 kB replies (messages, rendered rows, receipts). Auto-compaction bounds it: a longer variant of the same probe hit auto-summarization around turn 55 ("context at 10.0k/12.0k"), holding a ~27 MB plateau at that point (that run preloads all 300 canned responses into memory, so several MB of the plateau is fixture overhead).
  • A paste costs about 2.7 MB of editor state for 8 kB (+0.1 MB more on submit), freed again on submit.
  • Resume is cheap: a fresh process re-rendering a 14 kB transcript lands 0.3 MB above a fresh boot.

120-turn leak regression (issue #35)

tests/api/test_memory_leak.nim runs 120 real threaded-transport turns against a local HTTP server with usage numbers chosen to trip auto-summarization every ~10 turns, then asserts the RSS slope from turn 30 to the end stays under 5 MB. It now prints its measurement:

rss warmup 17192kB end 17208kB slope 16kB over 90 turns

This is the guard for the three leak classes that once made RSS grow forever on long sessions (per-summarizer SSL context leak, worker thread ORC leaks, cycle-table strands). 0.2 kB/turn of drift is allocator noise, not a leak.

Where the memory actually lives (census)

smaps of the probe child mid-session (turn 20, RSS 15.7 MB), largest resident mappings:

kB RSSMapping
5352anonymous rw (Nim ORC heap: message history, rendered rows)
19203code binary text (release, --opt:size, 4.9 MB on disk)
1536libcrypto.so.3 text
1392libc.so.6 text
696anonymous rw (second arena / stream buffers)
580+324+2403code binary rodata + relocated data

And the largest virtual reservations, which are the VSZ story:

kB SizekB RSSMapping
654040---p anonymous (glibc arena reservation, thread 2)
654040---p anonymous (glibc arena reservation, thread 3)
819284rw-p anonymous (thread stack)

So VSZ 165 MB decomposes as: 2 x 64 MB arena fences + 8 MB stack + heap + ~15 MB of libraries. glibc reserves each non-main arena as one 64 MB PROT_NONE region and commits pages inside it only as that thread mallocs. Nothing can be "freed" here; if VSZ bothers you, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 caps the count (at some lock contention cost), but RSS is unaffected.

Paste cost (the one real problem found)

Feeding a large single-line paste into the editor and submitting it is superlinear in wall time, though flat in memory. Timed with 30 ms-drain PTY feeding (1.8 kB pieces), stub provider, otherwise idle session:

PasteFeed timeSubmit-to-replyRSS after
1 kB1.0 s0.25 s+0.8 MB
2 kB2.1 s0.25 s+1.3 MB
4 kB3.2 s0.25 s+3.4 MB
8 kB5.2 s0.25 s+3.5 MB
16 kB10.7 s2.0 s+3.8 MB
32 kB22.4 s

5 s

+3.3 MB

(120 kB measured separately: about 60-90 s of child CPU to commit the echo, RSS still ~13 MB.) Both the per-piece editor reflow while pasting and the scrollback commit of the multi-thousand-column echo row grow faster than linear. Memory stays bounded; a big paste into 3code will not OOM you, but pasting a 100 kB log blob will pin a core for a minute. That is a render-path cost, not a leak, and it is the one finding here worth a follow-up issue.

Reproducing

# stub binary + probe (release config)
nim c --skipParentCfg --noNimblePath -d:release --opt:size \
  -p:src -p:tests -d:ssl -d:testPlainHttp -d:providerStub --threads:on \
  <dep paths> -o:/tmp/3code_stub src/threecode.nim
nim c --skipParentCfg --noNimblePath -p:src -p:tests -d:ssl \
  -d:testPlainHttp <dep paths> -o:/tmp/probe_ram tests/tty/probe_ram.nim
/tmp/probe_ram /tmp/3code_stub [turns=40] [idle-secs=75]

# leak regression (prints its slope now)
nim c -r tests/api/test_memory_leak.nim

Caveats: the stub provider replaces the network with canned in-process responses, so per-turn RSS deltas exclude real TLS/stream buffers (the live-session table above covers that side qualitatively). All numbers are one box, one run each; treat single-digit-kB differences as noise.
